## The three findings that matter

**F5.1 — a hard `undeclared-prereq` failure that no gate in this run could catch.** `def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations` cites `def-free-abelian-group` and `thm-abelianisation-of-a-free-group-is-free-abelian`, both homed on `free-groups-and-presentations` (order 60), which is not in order 106's closure. It's load-bearing — the universal-property contract opens "Let $F$ be the free abelian group on $M\times N$". It survived every gate because `validate-plan` skips published deps in the item loop (`if (existing.has(d)) continue;`) and induces page edges only from spec item lists — and that page carries 6 items in the spec against 32 on disk. Fix: cite `def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis` + `thm-universal-property-of-free-modules` at $R=\mathbb Z$, both on `free-modules-and-exact-sequences` (already the page's most-cited prerequisite). The published, judged `lem-every-abelian-group-embeds-in-a-divisible-group` uses exactly that move. **I swept all 450 items in all seven batches — this is the only out-of-closure dep in the run.**

**F1.1 — the Sylvester decline is real, but two declines beside it are false.** Your premise was wrong: determinants are order 82, `symmetric-polynomials` is 58, so that decline is structurally forced. But I opened Milne p. 58 and he doesn't define the resultant by a Sylvester matrix at all — it's $a^mb^n\prod_{i,j}(\alpha_i-\beta_j)$, and Prop 4.35(a) and (c) are proved from that with no determinant ("obvious"). Both were declined for a determinant reason that is false in the monic case. Three provable items lost, including one the design paragraph Beta replaced had explicitly listed.

**F2.1 — a skipped subsection hides the page's missing theorem.** Hackman's locator excludes §C.III. §C.III is "Binomial Congruences" and contains **C.III.1, Euler's Criterion** — general $m$, general $n$: $x^m\equiv a$ is solvable iff $a^{\varphi(n)/(\varphi(n),m)}\equiv1$. Its proof is exactly this page's index calculus. It's in no source's contents and no coverage row. The $m=2$/Legendre specialisation correctly belongs to `quadratic-residues-and-the-legendre-symbol` (57.003), but the general criterion belongs here.
